criteria.description: When fetch succeeds, favouriteIds retains the optimistically applied change: adding a product keeps it in the set; removing a product keeps it absent.
criteria.evidence: tests/favouriteRevert.test.tsx: all 4 tests passed — '✓ tests/favouriteRevert.test.tsx (4 tests) 226ms'. Full suite: 21 passed (21) across 7 files, exit code 0.

criteria.description: When fetch rejects, the catch block reverts the optimistic change for the affected product only: if wasAdded===true removes productId; if wasAdded===false re-adds productId.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx lines 75-85: catch block contains setFavouriteIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); if (wasAdded) { next.delete(productId); } else { next.add(productId); } return next; }) — conditionally adds/removes based on wasAdded.

criteria.description: The revert in the catch block uses a functional state updater (setFavouriteIds(prev => ...)) — not a captured snapshot.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx lines 76-84: setFavouriteIds((prev) => { ... }) — functional updater form confirmed; no captured snapshot used.

criteria.description: productId is added to pendingIds before the fetch call using a functional updater that does not mutate prev.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx line 61: setPendingIds((prev) => new Set(prev).add(productId)) appears after the optimistic setFavouriteIds update (lines 51-59) and before the fetch calls (lines 65-73). Functional updater confirmed; does not mutate prev.

criteria.description: productId is removed from pendingIds unconditionally inside a finally block; cleanup is not duplicated in try or catch.
criteria.evidence: FavouritesContext.tsx lines 86-91: finally block calls setPendingIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; }). No setPendingIds deletion in try or catch blocks — cleanup is only in finally.

criteria.description: The only file modified is src/context/FavouritesContext.tsx; FavouriteButton.tsx and FavouritesPage.tsx are unchanged.
criteria.evidence: git diff --name-only returned no output (clean working tree). FavouriteButton.tsx (33 lines) and FavouritesPage.tsx (31 lines) contain no optimistic-update or revert logic — they only consume context methods. All task logic is confined to FavouritesContext.tsx.
